title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt (Q4 2026) — the cut the March monthly's title wrongly absorbed, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,179 bytes) by the tic-monthly-2027-03-18 initial research — its 2027 table's March row reads '31' in the column headed 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt at end of previous quarter', a SEPARATE dated column from the '18' cells in the Monthly and Quarterly-derivatives columns. Under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference quarter Q4 2026 by the column's own 'at end of previous quarter' rule. Corroborated mechanically and exactly: 2027-03-31 is a Wednesday and is March 2027's LAST BUSINESS DAY, recomputed from scratch — matching the convention the same column follows in every regular quarter of both published years (2026: 03-31, 06-30, 09-30, 12-31; 2027: 03-31, 06-30, 09-30, 12-30), an offset of +0 with no slack, unlike the monthly release's '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days'. THE ONE EXCEPTION IN THE TABLE IS STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: the 2026 January row carries '16 (delayed)' in this same column — a Q3-2025 external-debt publication that slipped out of its own quarter entirely and landed mid-January, Treasury labelling it so on the page. So the last-business-day convention is exact where it holds and has visibly failed once in the eight quarters published, which is why this entry is filed estimate on its date as well as on the taxonomy. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep: the proposer may not confirm what it found, only the event's own session may. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-monthly-2027-03-18 initial research (2026-09-09) as the direct product of that session's title correction. The proposal that created tic-monthly-2027-03-18 titled it 'the March triple' by reading the 2027 row `18 | 18 | 31` as three cuts on one date. It is not: the '31' sits in a SEPARATE dated column and is THIS release, thirteen days later. That is the same separate-column-read-as-component error tic-monthly-2027-02-18 caught in its own proposal one row up (the preliminary annual survey publishing eight days after the monthly, not inside it) — the third instance of one misreading of one table, which is why the cut is filed as its own event rather than absorbed again. THE PRECEDENT REVERSAL IS STATED: tic-monthly-2027-02-18 explicitly DECLINED the 2027-03-31 external-debt cut on the ground that it carries 'no press release'. That precedent has since been superseded by tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-06-30, proposed the same day by the tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26 sweep on the identical column — so the family id pattern now exists and March is the unclaimed member of it. IT ALSO HAS A JOB. tic-monthly-2027-03-18 refuted 'March's multi-cut structure' as the mechanism behind FT-tic-monthly-2027-01-19-3's post-hoc Feb/Mar exclusion, by reading the quarterly column DOWN (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, four vintages a year) rather than the March row ACROSS. This event is the other half of that reading: the external-debt cut is likewise quarterly, so if any March-specific effect survives it must live in the monthly/derivatives pair on 03-18 and not in the month's cut count. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is a quarter stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed) and one more specific to this cut: gross external debt is a reconciliation statistic with no consensus distribution and no sell-side forecast. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
